chunks: [Categories of oppression:] Know that injustice is of three kinds: one that is not forgiven, one that is not left (unpunished), and one that is forgiven and not sought after.
As for the injustice that is not forgiven, it is duality (associating partners) with Allah. Allah the Exalted said: 'Verily Allah forgiveth not that (anything) be associated with Him'.
Verily Allah forgiveth not that (anything) be associated with Him
As for the injustice that is forgiven, it is the injustice a man does to himself by committing small sins; and the injustice that is not left (unpunished) is the injustice of men against other men.
The retribution in such a case is severe. It is not wounding with knives, nor striking with whips, but it is so severe that all these things are small against it.

You should therefore avoid change in the matter of Allah's religion, for indeed a group united upon what you dislike of the truth is better than a group scattered upon what you like of falsehood. And indeed Allah, Glorified is He, has not given any person, whether among those who passed away or among those who remain, any good from separation.

key_terms.الشِّرْكُ: Duality or associating partners with God

ai.seo_question: What are the three categories of injustice in Shia theology and how are they distinguished?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) delineates three categories of injustice, distinguishing between shirk as the unforgivable sin, self-harm through minor sins which is pardoned, and interpersonal injustice requiring strict retribution (qisas) that transcends physical penalties. He further links this taxonomy to the danger of innovation (bid'ah), warning that unity upon truth is superior to fragmentation upon falsehood, a key theme in Shia political theology regarding the preservation of the community's integrity.
